cities.name: Kaziranga
cities.overview: The floodplain grasslands of the Brahmaputra in Golaghat and Nagaon districts, reached from the gateway village of Kohora on the Guwahati–Jorhat highway.

cities.name: Guwahati
cities.overview: Assam's largest city and the gateway to Northeast India, spread along the south bank of the Brahmaputra.
cities.history: Ancient Pragjyotishpura, a seat of old Assamese kingdoms on the Brahmaputra. The Ahoms held it after defeating the Mughals at the Battle of Saraighat in 1671, and today it's the gateway to the Northeast.

cities.name: Majuli
cities.overview: A large river island in the Brahmaputra, reached by ferry from Nimati Ghat near Jorhat, and the centre of Assam's Vaishnavite satra culture.

cities.name: Sivasagar
cities.overview: The old capital of the Ahom kingdom, full of brick palaces, temples and royal tanks.
cities.history: The Ahoms ruled Assam for around 600 years, and they governed from here in the 18th century.

cities.name: Tezpur
cities.overview: A pretty town on the Brahmaputra, known for its old legends and close to the forests of Nameri.

cities.name: Jorhat
cities.overview: A tea town in upper Assam, close to Majuli and the gibbon sanctuary.

cities.name: Barpeta
cities.overview: A western town known for its Vaishnavite monastery and as the gateway to Manas.

cities.name: Tinsukia
cities.overview: A tea town in the far east of Assam, close to Dibru-Saikhowa.

cities.name: Haflong
cities.overview: Assam's only hill station, in the Dima Hasao hills.

places.name: Kaziranga National Park
places.shortDescription: A UNESCO-listed park of tall grass and wetlands, home to most of the world's greater one-horned rhinoceroses.
places.description: Kaziranga's elephant grass, marshes and forest along the Brahmaputra shelter the world's largest population of greater one-horned rhinoceroses, along with wild water buffalo, swamp deer, elephants and one of the highest densities of tigers anywhere. Jeep safaris run in four ranges, Central (Kohora) being the most popular, and early-morning elephant rides operate in some ranges. Birdlife is rich, especially in winter. The park closes during the monsoon floods.
places.history: Kaziranga was set aside as a reserve forest in 1908 to protect the dwindling rhino, became a national park in 1974 and was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985.
places.bestTimeNote: November to April. The park is usually closed from May to October for the monsoon.

entryFee.note: Entry and jeep safari permits are charged separately by range; book through the Assam Forest Department.

timings.hours: Safaris in morning and afternoon slots

highlights: Jeep safari in the Central range
Wild water buffalo and swamp deer

places.name: Kamakhya Temple
places.shortDescription: One of India's most important Shakti Peethas, on Nilachal Hill above Guwahati.
places.description: The Kamakhya Temple is dedicated to the mother goddess Kamakhya and is a major centre of Tantric worship. Its beehive-shaped shikhara and the cluster of smaller shrines to the ten Mahavidyas crown Nilachal Hill. There is no idol in the inner sanctum: devotees worship a natural spring-fed stone. Queues can be long; a paid fast-track queue is available. The annual Ambubachi Mela in June draws huge crowds when the temple shuts for three days.
places.history: The present structure was rebuilt in the 16th century by the Koch king Nara Narayana after an earlier temple was destroyed. It is counted among the 51 Shakti Peethas in Hindu tradition.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March. Ambubachi Mela (June) and Navratri are the busiest times.

entryFee.note: Free general queue; paid special-entry queue available.

timings.hours: About 5:30 AM – 10:00 PM, with closures around midday rituals

places.name: Majuli
places.shortDescription: A large river island in the Brahmaputra, dotted with Vaishnavite satras, mask-makers and Mising villages.
places.description: Majuli is a flat, green island of rice fields, wetlands and stilt houses, reached by a river ferry from Nimati Ghat near Jorhat. Its satras, monasteries of the neo-Vaishnavite tradition founded by Srimanta Sankardeva, keep alive sattriya dance, devotional music and the craft of mask-making, best seen at Samaguri Satra. Cycling between villages is the nicest way to explore. Erosion by the Brahmaputra has shrunk the island considerably over the past century.
places.history: Sankardeva and his disciple Madhavdeva met on Majuli in the early 16th century, and dozens of satras were founded here in the centuries after. Majuli became India's first island district in 2016.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March. The Raas Mahotsav in November is a highlight; monsoon floods disrupt travel.

places.name: Umananda Temple
places.shortDescription: A Shiva temple on the smallest inhabited river island in the world, in the Brahmaputra at Guwahati.
places.description: A short ferry ride takes you to a small wooded island in the river, a lovely trip in its own right, especially at sunset.

places.name: Srimanta Sankardev Kalakshetra
places.shortDescription: A cultural complex in Guwahati, showing the arts and traditions of Assam.
places.description: A museum, open-air theatre and art gallery that give a good introduction to the Sattriya dance and the region's many cultures.

places.name: Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A small grassland near Guwahati, with one of the world's densest populations of one-horned rhinos.
places.description: An easy half-day from the city. You've got a very good chance of seeing a rhino here on an elephant or jeep safari.

places.name: Hajo
places.shortDescription: A historic pilgrim town near Guwahati, sacred to Hindus, Buddhists and Muslims.
places.description: Hajo holds the Hayagriva Madhava Temple, which some Buddhists also revere, and Poa Mecca, a mosque that's said to hold a quarter of the holiness of Mecca.

places.name: Manas National Park
places.shortDescription: A UNESCO World Heritage park in the Himalayan foothills, with tigers, golden langurs and pygmy hogs.
places.description: Riverine forest and tall grass on the Bhutan border. It came back from serious damage to become a showpiece of recovery.

places.name: Nameri National Park
places.shortDescription: A forest on the Jia Bhoreli River, one of the few parks in India you can walk or raft through.
places.description: Guided walks and rafting on the river bring you close to many birds, including white-winged wood duck. It's great for birders.

places.name: Agnigarh
places.shortDescription: A hillock at Tezpur linked with the Hindu legend of Usha and Aniruddha, with river views.
places.description: Steps and sculptures climb to a viewpoint over the Brahmaputra. Tezpur's Kolia Bhomora Setu bridge is visible from the top.

places.name: Orang National Park
places.shortDescription: A smaller version of Kaziranga, on the north bank of the Brahmaputra, with rhinos and tigers.
places.description: Sometimes called Mini Kaziranga, it's far quieter than its famous neighbour. Grassland and water make for good rhino sightings.

places.name: Rang Ghar
places.shortDescription: A two-storey royal pavilion of the Ahoms, from which kings watched buffalo fights and games.
places.description: An oval pavilion with a roof in the shape of a boat. It's among the oldest surviving sports pavilions in Asia.
places.history: Built by the Ahom king Swargadeo Pramatta Singha in the 18th century.

places.name: Talatal Ghar
places.shortDescription: The largest Ahom monument, a brick palace with underground levels at Rangpur.
places.description: A big, seven-storey palace, partly hidden below ground, near Sivasagar. Most of the lower floors are now sealed.
places.history: An 18th-century royal palace and military base.

places.name: Sivadol
places.shortDescription: A tall Shiva temple by the Sivasagar tank, among the tallest in India.
places.description: A set of three Ahom temples on a large man-made lake, built by Queen Ambika. The Sivadol's tall tower is the landmark.

places.name: Hollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A small forest near Jorhat and the only place in India with the hoolock gibbon, the only ape.
places.description: A walk with a forest guide through the tall hollong trees, listening for the gibbons' loud morning songs.

places.name: Dibru-Saikhowa National Park
places.shortDescription: A wet grassland on the Brahmaputra with feral horses, and a key spot for rare birds.
places.description: Boat trips across the river channels lead into forest and grass, home to rare white-winged duck, feral horses and river dolphins.

places.name: Haflong Lake
places.shortDescription: A hill town in Dima Hasao, Assam's only hill station, with a lake and paragliding.
places.description: Dima Hasao's blue hills surround a small lake in town. Nearby Jatinga is known for a mystery in which birds fly into its lights.
